canonical_statement: A sequence of probability measures satisfies the large deviation principle with a positive speed tending to infinity and a nonnegative lower-semicontinuous rate function when every closed set has the corresponding exponential upper bound and every open set has the corresponding exponential lower bound.
domain_and_universes: E : Type u with topological and measurable structures; n : Nat; events s : Set E; extended-real rates
quantifiers: a sequence of probability measures mu_n on E
a positive speed a_n tending to infinity
a nonnegative lower-semicontinuous rate function I : E -> extended real
every closed F and every open G
hypotheses: each mu_n is a probability measure
0 < a_n and a_n tends to infinity
topological and measurable structures support probabilities of the tested events
conclusion: limsup_n (1/a_n) log(mu_n(F)) <= -inf_{x in F} I(x) for closed F, and -inf_{x in G} I(x) <= liminf_n (1/a_n) log(mu_n(G)) for open G
boundary_cases: probability zero uses log 0 = negative infinity
the infimum over the empty event follows the selected extended-real convention
a good rate function adds compact sublevel sets and is not part of the base property
a weak LDP tests compact upper-bound sets and is not substituted for the full LDP
excluded_claims: No universal assertion that arbitrary measures satisfy an LDP; no Cramer, Gartner-Ellis, Sanov, Varadhan, moderate-deviation, weak-LDP, or good-rate-function theorem.
